history.p: Gade wrote his eighth symphony during the winter 1869-1870 and orchestrated it in the summer of 1870. During a visit to the Beethoven celebrations in Bonn in 1871, he told his friends about his new work. Ferdinand Hiller wanted to conduct the first performance in Cologne, but Gade wanted to try it out for himself before it was released for performance. This took place in Copenhagen on 7 December 1871. The symphony was well received in Denmark and abroad, but although Gade lived another twenty years, this remained his last symphony.

physDesc.physMedium: 1 bifolio and 12 single folios. Written in ink with numerous corrections in pencil. Partly paginated. The first movement is end-dated "comp. Febr 1870" and Gade's musical signature and the Finale "15 April / 2. Juli 70". Contains sketches for all four movements, a discarded Allegretto and "Aarstidsbilleder" (NWGW 175).

physDesc.physMedium: 16 bifolios and 4 single folios. Written in ink with many emendations in pencil. Paper: 12 and 14 staves. Paginated 1-72, but some of the original numberings have been changed. Numerous corrections and discarded passages. At the bottom of p. 72 Gade has written: "Comp: i Vinteren 1869 - 70. Instrumenteret Juli & August 1870 / (Jægersborg.)".

physLoc.identifier: C II, 6 Gades Samling 394 (Kapsel St - Sø)

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in green cardboard cover with green cloth spine. In upper left-hand corner a handwritten label inscribed: "Symphonie No 8 / op. 47. "Written in ink. Paper: 18 staves. Paginated 1-100; p. 52 blank. Rehearsal letters added in blue crayon in each movement. At the end of the Finale Gade has written: "Componeret Vinteren 1869-70. / Instrumenteret Sommeren 1870. / Færdig instrumenteret October 1871. / (Christiansborg og Vestergade No 2) / Første Gang opført / d. 7de December 1871".
